```{r}
# rbind() creates a 3-row data frame with all results combined
#
# HEALTH ECONOMIC VALUE:
# Creates a single table for Table 2 in the manuscript, showing all countries
# side-by-side for easy comparison of cost-effectiveness across settings

# Check if any country data was loaded
# -------------------------------------
# length(psa_list) returns the number of elements in the list
# If 0, no country files were found → display warning and skip consolidation
# If ≥1, proceed with combining available data
#
# Defensive programming: Prevents errors from trying to combine empty list
if (length(psa_list) == 0) {

  # WARNING MESSAGE:
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Alerts the user that no PSA summary files were found
  # Provides guidance on how to generate the required files
  #
  # Health economic interpretation: Cannot consolidate results until individual
  # country PSAs have been run
  cat("\n⚠ WARNING: No PSA summary files found!\n")
  cat("\nTo generate PSA summaries:\n")
  cat("1. Uncomment the Ireland country block and run the PSA section\n")
  cat("2. Uncomment the Germany country block and run the PSA section\n")
  cat("3. Uncomment the Spain country block and run the PSA section\n")
  cat("4. Re-run this consolidation chunk\n\n")

  # Create empty placeholder to avoid errors in subsequent code
  # This data frame has the correct column structure but zero rows
  psa_consolidated <- data.frame(
    Country = character(),
    WTP_Threshold = numeric(),
    Incremental_Cost_Mean = numeric(),
    Incremental_Cost_Lower_CrI = numeric(),
    Incremental_Cost_Upper_CrI = numeric(),
    Incremental_QALY_Mean = numeric(),
    Incremental_QALY_Lower_CrI = numeric(),
    Incremental_QALY_Upper_CrI = numeric(),
    Incremental_NMB_Mean = numeric(),
    Incremental_NMB_Lower_CrI = numeric(),
    Incremental_NMB_Upper_CrI = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

} else {

  # COMBINE AVAILABLE COUNTRY DATA:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # do.call(rbind, psa_list) stacks all available country data frames vertically
  #
  # If all 3 countries available → 3-row table
  # If only 2 countries available → 2-row table
  # If only 1 country available → 1-row table
  #
  # Health economic interpretation: Creating consolidated PSA summary table
  # with incremental costs, QALYs, and NMB (with 95% CrIs) for each country
  psa_consolidated <- do.call(rbind, psa_list)

  # Reset row names to simple sequential numbering
  # -----------------------------------------------
  # By default, rbind() preserves row names from original data frames
  # This can create messy row names like "Ireland.1", "Germany.1", etc.
  # Setting row.names = NULL creates clean sequential numbering (1, 2, 3...)
  #
  # Cosmetic improvement for cleaner output
  row.names(psa_consolidated) <- NULL

  # Confirm successful consolidation
  # ---------------------------------
  # Shows how many countries were included in the consolidated table
  # This serves as a quality check (should match number of files found)
  cat("\n✓ Successfully consolidated results from", nrow(psa_consolidated), "country/countries\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: DISPLAY CONSOLIDATED RAW TABLE
# ============================================================================
#
# TABLE DISPLAY PURPOSE:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shows the consolidated results in the R console for immediate review
#
# WHY DISPLAY THE RAW TABLE?
# 1. Immediate verification that consolidation worked correctly
# 2. Check that all countries are included
# 3. Verify WTP thresholds are correct for each country
# 4. Spot-check that numerical values are sensible (no obvious errors)
#
# INTERPRETATION GUIDANCE:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# When reviewing this table, check:
#
# FOR INCREMENTAL COSTS:
# - Should be positive (bevacizumab is expensive → adds costs)
# - Magnitude should be in €20,000-€40,000 range (biologic therapy cost)
# - CrI width reflects cost uncertainty
#
# FOR INCREMENTAL QALYs:
# - Should be small positive values (survival extension is modest)
# - Typically 0.1-0.3 QALYs (a few months of life extension)
# - CrI width reflects survival benefit uncertainty
#
# FOR INCREMENTAL NMB:
# - May be positive or negative depending on WTP threshold and country
# - Negative NMB → costs exceed value of health benefits
# - If entire CrI is negative → strong evidence against cost-effectiveness
# - If CrI spans zero → uncertain cost-effectiveness

# Display consolidated table header
# ----------------------------------
cat("=======================================================\n")
cat("CONSOLIDATED PSA SUMMARY (RAW DATA - FULL PRECISION)\n")
cat("=======================================================\n\n")

# Display the data frame
# ----------------------
# print() shows the table in standard R format
# All numeric values displayed with full precision
#
# Health economic value: Transparent reporting of exact numerical results
# for peer review and reproducibility
if (nrow(psa_consolidated) > 0) {
  print(psa_consolidated, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n")
} else {
  cat("(No data to display - PSA summaries not yet generated)\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: CREATE FORMATTED VERSION FOR MANUSCRIPT
# ============================================================================
#
# FORMATTING PURPOSE:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The raw table above is ideal for analysis but not publication-ready.
# This formatted version applies:
# 1. Currency symbols (€)
# 2. Thousand separators (€12,345)
# 3. Appropriate rounding (costs to €1, QALYs to 4 decimals)
# 4. Combined "mean (95% CrI)" presentation
#
# FORMATTING APPROACH:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We apply formatting only if data exists (nrow > 0)
# For each metric, we create human-readable text combining mean and CrI
#
# HEALTH ECONOMIC VALUE:
# Publication-ready table following standard reporting conventions for
# cost-effectiveness analyses (aligned with CHEERS checklist)

# Only create formatted table if we have data
# --------------------------------------------
if (nrow(psa_consolidated) > 0) {

  # Create formatted version of consolidated table
  # -----------------------------------------------
  # data.frame() constructs a new table with formatted text columns
  #
  # Each row corresponds to one country from psa_consolidated
  # psa_consolidated$Column_Name accesses that column's values
  #
  # FORMATTING FUNCTIONS USED:
  # - round(x, n): Round to n decimal places
  # - format(x, big.mark = ","): Add thousand separators
  # - paste0(): Concatenate strings without separator
  #
  # Health economic interpretation: Converting raw numerical results into
  # publication-ready formatted text for manuscript Table 2
  psa_consolidated_formatted <- data.frame(

    # Country column: unchanged (already text)
    # -----------------------------------------
    # Simply copies the country name from raw table
    Country = psa_consolidated$Country,

    # WTP threshold: formatted with currency symbol and separators
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Example: 45000 → "€45,000"
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Shows the societal willingness-to-pay
    # threshold used to calculate NMB for each country
    `WTP Threshold` = paste0("€", format(psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold, big.mark = ",")),

    # Incremental cost: formatted as "Mean (95% CrI)"
    # -----------------------------------------------
    # Example: "€30,847 (€22,086 to €40,747)"
    #
    # FORMAT BREAKDOWN:
    # 1. round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_Cost_Mean, 0): Round mean to nearest €1
    # 2. format(..., big.mark = ","): Add thousand separators
    # 3. paste0("€", ...): Add currency symbol
    # 4. Repeat for lower and upper CrI bounds
    # 5. Combine with " (" and " to " separators
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Expected additional cost of bevacizumab
    # with 95% credible interval showing cost uncertainty
    `Incremental Cost (Mean and 95% CrI)` = paste0(
      "€", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_Cost_Mean, 0), big.mark = ","),
      " (€", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_Cost_Lower_CrI, 0), big.mark = ","),
      " to €", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_Cost_Upper_CrI, 0), big.mark = ","), ")"
    ),

    # Incremental QALY: formatted as "Mean (95% CrI)"
    # -----------------------------------------------
    # Example: "0.1709 (0.0664 to 0.2894)"
    #
    # FORMAT BREAKDOWN:
    # 1. round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_QALY_Mean, 4): Round to 4 decimal places
    #    (standard precision for QALYs)
    # 2. No currency symbol or thousand separators (QALYs are small numbers)
    # 3. Combine with " (" and " to " separators
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Expected health gain from bevacizumab
    # in quality-adjusted life years, with 95% credible interval showing
    # uncertainty in the survival benefit
    `Incremental QALY (Mean and 95% CrI)` = paste0(
      round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_QALY_Mean, 4),
      " (", round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_QALY_Lower_CrI, 4),
      " to ", round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_QALY_Upper_CrI, 4), ")"
    ),

    # Incremental NMB: formatted as "Mean (95% CrI)"
    # ----------------------------------------------
    # Example: "€-23,155 (€-30,496 to €-16,773)"
    #
    # FORMAT BREAKDOWN:
    # Same as incremental cost (currency symbol, thousand separators, rounded to €1)
    #
    # SPECIAL HANDLING OF NEGATIVE VALUES:
    # When NMB is negative, the minus sign appears after the € symbol: "€-23,155"
    # This is a formatting quirk but doesn't affect interpretation
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Expected net monetary benefit of bevacizumab
    # at the country-specific WTP threshold, with 95% credible interval
    #
    # DECISION RULE:
    # - Positive NMB → intervention may be cost-effective
    # - Negative NMB → intervention may not be cost-effective
    # - If entire CrI is negative → strong evidence against cost-effectiveness
    `Incremental NMB (Mean and 95% CrI)` = paste0(
      "€", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean, 0), big.mark = ","),
      " (€", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Lower_CrI, 0), big.mark = ","),
      " to €", format(round(psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Upper_CrI, 0), big.mark = ","), ")"
    ),

    # Preserve column names exactly as specified
    # -------------------------------------------
    # check.names = FALSE: Don't convert spaces/parentheses to dots
    # Without this, R would change "WTP Threshold" to "WTP.Threshold"
    check.names = FALSE,

    # Keep text as character strings, not factors
    # --------------------------------------------
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Display formatted consolidated table
  # -------------------------------------
  # This is the publication-ready version for manuscript Table 2
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("CONSOLIDATED PSA SUMMARY (FORMATTED FOR MANUSCRIPT)\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n\n")
  print(psa_consolidated_formatted, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n")

} else {
  # No data available message
  # --------------------------
  cat("\n(Formatted table not created - no PSA data available)\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: SAVE CONSOLIDATED TABLES TO CSV FILES
# ============================================================================
#
# FILE OUTPUT PURPOSE:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We save TWO versions of the consolidated table:
#
# 1. RAW VERSION (PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries.csv):
#    - Full numerical precision
#    - Suitable for further analysis
#    - Can import into R for calculations
#
# 2. FORMATTED VERSION (PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries_Formatted.csv):
#    - Publication-ready formatting
#    - Currency symbols and thousand separators
#    - Ready to copy into manuscript Word document
#
# FILE ORGANIZATION:
# Both files saved to output/ directory alongside individual country files
#
# VERSION CONTROL:
# CSV files can be tracked in Git to monitor how results change over time
#
# REPRODUCIBILITY:
# Permanent record of consolidated PSA results for all countries

# Save raw consolidated table (if data exists)
# --------------------------------------------
if (nrow(psa_consolidated) > 0) {

  # Define output file path
  # -----------------------
  # file.path() creates platform-independent path
  consolidated_raw_file <- file.path("output", "PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries.csv")

  # Write to CSV
  # ------------
  # row.names = FALSE: Don't include row numbers in CSV
  # This makes the file cleaner and easier to import into other tools
  #
  # Health economic value: Preserves full numerical precision for
  # transparent reporting and reproducibility
  write.csv(psa_consolidated, file = consolidated_raw_file, row.names = FALSE)

  # Confirm successful save with file path
  cat("✓ Raw consolidated table saved to:", consolidated_raw_file, "\n")
}

# Save formatted consolidated table (if data exists)
# ---------------------------------------------------
if (nrow(psa_consolidated) > 0) {

  # Define output file path
  # -----------------------
  consolidated_formatted_file <- file.path("output", "PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries_Formatted.csv")

  # Write to CSV
  # ------------
  # Same parameters as raw table above
  #
  # Health economic value: Publication-ready formatted output that can be
  # directly copied into manuscript Table 2, reducing transcription errors
  write.csv(psa_consolidated_formatted, file = consolidated_formatted_file, row.names = FALSE)

  # Confirm successful save with file path
  cat("✓ Formatted consolidated table saved to:", consolidated_formatted_file, "\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: PROVIDE PLAIN-LANGUAGE INTERPRETATION OF RESULTS
# ============================================================================
#
# INTERPRETATION PURPOSE:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Translates statistical results into decision-relevant findings that
# stakeholders (clinicians, policymakers, patients) can understand.
#
# FOCUS AREAS:
# 1. Overall cost-effectiveness conclusion (is NMB positive or negative?)
# 2. Strength of evidence (how wide are the credible intervals?)
# 3. Consistency across countries (do all countries reach same conclusion?)
# 4. Impact of WTP threshold (how sensitive are results to threshold choice?)
#
# HEALTH ECONOMIC VALUE:
# Makes technical PSA results accessible to non-specialist audiences

# Only provide interpretation if we have data
# --------------------------------------------
if (nrow(psa_consolidated) > 0) {

  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("PLAIN-LANGUAGE INTERPRETATION OF PSA RESULTS\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n\n")

  # INTERPRETATION 1: Overall cost-effectiveness by country
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  cat("1. COST-EFFECTIVENESS CONCLUSIONS:\n")
  cat("-----------------------------------\n\n")

  # Loop through each country to provide specific interpretation
  # -------------------------------------------------------------
  # for loop iterates through each row of the consolidated table
  # i takes values 1, 2, 3 (or fewer if not all countries available)
  for (i in 1:nrow(psa_consolidated)) {

    # Extract values for this country
    # --------------------------------
    # Makes code more readable by assigning clear variable names
    country <- psa_consolidated$Country[i]
    wtp <- psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold[i]
    nmb_mean <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean[i]
    nmb_lower <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Lower_CrI[i]
    nmb_upper <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Upper_CrI[i]

    # Country-specific interpretation based on NMB sign and CrI
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    cat(country, "(WTP = €", format(wtp, big.mark = ","), "):\n", sep = "")

    # CASE 1: Entire 95% CrI is below zero (strong evidence AGAINST)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Both lower and upper bounds are negative
    # → 95% confident that NMB is negative
    # → Strong evidence that intervention is NOT cost-effective
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Very high confidence that costs exceed
    # benefits when valued at the WTP threshold
    if (nmb_upper < 0) {
      cat("  → Mean NMB is €", format(round(nmb_mean, 0), big.mark = ","), " (NEGATIVE)\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → 95% CrI entirely below zero: [€", format(round(nmb_lower, 0), big.mark = ","),
          " to €", format(round(nmb_upper, 0), big.mark = ","), "]\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → INTERPRETATION: Strong evidence that bevacizumab is NOT cost-effective\n")
      cat("     at the €", format(wtp, big.mark = ","), " WTP threshold.\n", sep = "")
      cat("     We are 95% confident that costs exceed the value of health benefits.\n")
      cat("     Bevacizumab should NOT be adopted at this threshold.\n\n")

    # CASE 2: Entire 95% CrI is above zero (strong evidence FOR)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Both lower and upper bounds are positive
    # → 95% confident that NMB is positive
    # → Strong evidence that intervention IS cost-effective
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Very high confidence that benefits
    # (valued at WTP) exceed costs
    } else if (nmb_lower > 0) {
      cat("  → Mean NMB is €", format(round(nmb_mean, 0), big.mark = ","), " (POSITIVE)\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → 95% CrI entirely above zero: [€", format(round(nmb_lower, 0), big.mark = ","),
          " to €", format(round(nmb_upper, 0), big.mark = ","), "]\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → INTERPRETATION: Strong evidence that bevacizumab IS cost-effective\n")
      cat("     at the €", format(wtp, big.mark = ","), " WTP threshold.\n", sep = "")
      cat("     We are 95% confident that health benefits (valued at WTP) exceed costs.\n")
      cat("     Bevacizumab SHOULD be adopted at this threshold.\n\n")

    # CASE 3: 95% CrI spans zero (uncertain cost-effectiveness)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Lower bound is negative, upper bound is positive
    # → Cannot rule out either positive or negative NMB
    # → Uncertain whether intervention is cost-effective
    #
    # Health economic interpretation: Decision uncertainty is high
    # May warrant value of information analysis to determine if further
    # research could reduce uncertainty and improve decision-making
    } else {
      # Determine if mean is positive or negative
      nmb_direction <- ifelse(nmb_mean > 0, "POSITIVE", "NEGATIVE")

      cat("  → Mean NMB is €", format(round(nmb_mean, 0), big.mark = ","), " (", nmb_direction, ")\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → 95% CrI spans zero: [€", format(round(nmb_lower, 0), big.mark = ","),
          " to €", format(round(nmb_upper, 0), big.mark = ","), "]\n", sep = "")
      cat("  → INTERPRETATION: UNCERTAIN cost-effectiveness at the €",
          format(wtp, big.mark = ","), " WTP threshold.\n", sep = "")
      cat("     The mean NMB is ", nmb_direction, ", but the credible interval includes both\n", sep = "")
      cat("     positive and negative values, indicating substantial decision uncertainty.\n")
      cat("     Additional research may be warranted to reduce uncertainty.\n")
      cat("     Consider value of information analysis.\n\n")
    }
  }

  # INTERPRETATION 2: Consistency across countries
  # -----------------------------------------------
  cat("\n2. CONSISTENCY ACROSS COUNTRIES:\n")
  cat("----------------------------------\n\n")

  # Count how many countries have negative mean NMB
  # ------------------------------------------------
  # sum() counts TRUE values
  # psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean < 0 creates logical vector
  n_negative <- sum(psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean < 0)
  n_total <- nrow(psa_consolidated)

  # Interpret consistency
  # ---------------------
  if (n_negative == n_total) {
    # All countries have negative NMB
    cat("All", n_total, "countries show NEGATIVE mean NMB.\n")
    cat("→ Cost-effectiveness conclusion is CONSISTENT across countries.\n")
    cat("→ Bevacizumab does NOT appear cost-effective in any of the analyzed settings,\n")
    cat("  despite differences in costs, WTP thresholds, and healthcare systems.\n\n")

  } else if (n_negative == 0) {
    # All countries have positive NMB
    cat("All", n_total, "countries show POSITIVE mean NMB.\n")
    cat("→ Cost-effectiveness conclusion is CONSISTENT across countries.\n")
    cat("→ Bevacizumab appears cost-effective in all analyzed settings,\n")
    cat("  despite differences in costs, WTP thresholds, and healthcare systems.\n\n")

  } else {
    # Mixed results across countries
    cat(n_negative, "out of", n_total, "countries show NEGATIVE mean NMB.\n")
    cat("→ Cost-effectiveness conclusions DIFFER across countries.\n")
    cat("→ Country-specific factors (costs, WTP threshold, healthcare system)\n")
    cat("  substantially affect cost-effectiveness.\n")
    cat("→ Decision-making should be country-specific rather than assuming\n")
    cat("  results transfer directly across settings.\n\n")
  }

  # INTERPRETATION 3: Parameter uncertainty
  # ----------------------------------------
  cat("\n3. PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY (WIDTH OF CREDIBLE INTERVALS):\n")
  cat("---------------------------------------------------------\n\n")

  # Calculate CrI width for NMB for each country
  # ---------------------------------------------
  # Width = Upper bound - Lower bound
  # Wider intervals → more uncertainty
  # Narrower intervals → more precise estimates
  for (i in 1:nrow(psa_consolidated)) {
    country <- psa_consolidated$Country[i]
    nmb_lower <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Lower_CrI[i]
    nmb_upper <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Upper_CrI[i]
    nmb_width <- nmb_upper - nmb_lower

    cat(country, ":\n", sep = "")
    cat("  95% CrI width for NMB: €", format(round(nmb_width, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n", sep = "")

    # Interpret width
    # ---------------
    # These thresholds are somewhat arbitrary but provide guidance
    if (nmb_width < 10000) {
      cat("  → Relatively NARROW credible interval (low uncertainty)\n")
      cat("     We have reasonably precise estimates of cost-effectiveness.\n\n")
    } else if (nmb_width < 20000) {
      cat("  → MODERATE credible interval width (moderate uncertainty)\n")
      cat("     Parameter uncertainty has a noticeable impact on results.\n\n")
    } else {
      cat("  → WIDE credible interval (high uncertainty)\n")
      cat("     Substantial parameter uncertainty affects cost-effectiveness estimates.\n")
      cat("     Results should be interpreted with caution.\n\n")
    }
  }

  # INTERPRETATION 4: Impact of WTP threshold
  # ------------------------------------------
  cat("\n4. IMPACT OF WILLINGNESS-TO-PAY THRESHOLD:\n")
  cat("--------------------------------------------\n\n")

  # Show how WTP thresholds differ across countries
  # ------------------------------------------------
  if (n_total > 1) {
    # Find country with lowest and highest WTP
    min_wtp_idx <- which.min(psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold)
    max_wtp_idx <- which.max(psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold)

    min_wtp_country <- psa_consolidated$Country[min_wtp_idx]
    min_wtp_value <- psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold[min_wtp_idx]
    min_wtp_nmb <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean[min_wtp_idx]

    max_wtp_country <- psa_consolidated$Country[max_wtp_idx]
    max_wtp_value <- psa_consolidated$WTP_Threshold[max_wtp_idx]
    max_wtp_nmb <- psa_consolidated$Incremental_NMB_Mean[max_wtp_idx]

    cat("WTP threshold ranges from €", format(min_wtp_value, big.mark = ","),
        " (", min_wtp_country, ")\n", sep = "")
    cat("                        to €", format(max_wtp_value, big.mark = ","),
        " (", max_wtp_country, ")\n\n", sep = "")

    cat("At LOWER WTP threshold (€", format(min_wtp_value, big.mark = ","), "):\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Mean NMB = €", format(round(min_wtp_nmb, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n\n", sep = "")

    cat("At HIGHER WTP threshold (€", format(max_wtp_value, big.mark = ","), "):\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Mean NMB = €", format(round(max_wtp_nmb, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n\n", sep = "")

    # Interpret WTP sensitivity
    # --------------------------
    # Higher WTP should lead to more positive (or less negative) NMB
    # because we're valuing health benefits more highly
    if (max_wtp_nmb > min_wtp_nmb) {
      cat("→ As expected, NMB is more favorable at higher WTP thresholds.\n")
      cat("  This is because we value health benefits (QALYs) more highly.\n")

      # Check if threshold changes decision
      if (min_wtp_nmb < 0 && max_wtp_nmb > 0) {
        cat("  IMPORTANT: The WTP threshold CHANGES THE DECISION.\n")
        cat("  Bevacizumab is NOT cost-effective at lower WTP but IS cost-effective at higher WTP.\n")
        cat("  Decision-making depends critically on societal WTP threshold.\n\n")
      } else {
        cat("  However, the WTP threshold does NOT change the overall decision\n")
        cat("  (both thresholds lead to the same conclusion about cost-effectiveness).\n\n")
      }
    }
  } else {
    cat("Only one country analyzed - cannot assess WTP threshold sensitivity across countries.\n\n")
  }

  cat("=======================================================\n\n")

} else {
  cat("\n(No interpretation provided - PSA data not yet available)\n\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# SECTION COMPLETE: CONSOLIDATED PSA REPORTING
# ============================================================================
#
# SUMMARY OF WHAT THIS SECTION ACCOMPLISHED:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. ✓ Checked for available country PSA summary files
# 2. ✓ Loaded all available country results
# 3. ✓ Combined into consolidated table (raw and formatted versions)
# 4. ✓ Displayed results in console with full documentation
# 5. ✓ Saved consolidated tables to CSV files
# 6. ✓ Provided plain-language interpretation of findings
#
# FILES CREATED (in output/ directory):
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# - PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries.csv
#   * Raw data with full numerical precision
#   * All countries combined in one table
#   * Suitable for further analysis
#
# - PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries_Formatted.csv
#   * Publication-ready formatted version
#   * Currency symbols, thousand separators, appropriate rounding
#   * Ready to copy into manuscript Table 2
#
# NEXT STEPS FOR MANUSCRIPT:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The consolidated formatted table can be directly used for:
# - Table 2 in the main manuscript (PSA-based cost-effectiveness results)
# - Supplementary tables showing country-specific results
# - Discussion of cross-country transferability
# - Justification of decision uncertainty and need for further research
#
# ALIGNMENT WITH REVIEWER 2 REQUEST:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This section addresses Reviewer 2's request to:
# ✓ Treat PSA as the effective base-case for decision-making
# ✓ Report net monetary benefit (NMB) as the primary outcome
# ✓ Provide credible intervals (95% CrI) for all incremental outcomes
# ✓ Create tables suitable for updated Table 2 in the manuscript
# ✓ Provide clear interpretation of cost-effectiveness conclusions
#
# The existing PSA (10,000 replications with appropriate distributions)
# is already methodologically sound and meets best practice standards.
# This consolidation section simply brings the results together for
# clear reporting and interpretation.

```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# CONSOLIDATE WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA RESULTS ACROSS ALL COUNTRIES
# =============================================================================
#
# OVERVIEW:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This chunk consolidates the Weibull vs Gamma PSA comparison results from all
# three countries (Ireland, Germany, Spain) into a single table. This mirrors
# the approach used for PSA_Summary_NMB_All_Countries but focuses on the
# structural uncertainty analysis comparing distributional assumptions.
#
# WORKFLOW (must be completed BEFORE running this chunk):
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Uncomment Ireland country block → Run PSA → Generates:
#   - output/Weibull_vs_Gamma_Ireland_PSA.csv
#
# STEP 2: Uncomment Germany country block → Run PSA → Generates:
#   - output/Weibull_vs_Gamma_Germany_PSA.csv
#
# STEP 3: Uncomment Spain country block → Run PSA → Generates:
#   - output/Weibull_vs_Gamma_Spain_PSA.csv
#
# STEP 4: Run THIS chunk → Consolidates all country results into:
#   - output/Weibull_vs_Gamma_All_Countries_PSA.csv
#
# HEALTH ECONOMIC INTERPRETATION:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The consolidated table allows assessment of:
#
# 1. STRUCTURAL UNCERTAINTY ACROSS COUNTRIES:
#    Does the choice between Weibull and Gamma distributions affect
#    cost-effectiveness conclusions differently across healthcare systems?
#
# 2. ROBUSTNESS OF DISTRIBUTIONAL CHOICE:
#    If both distributions yield similar results across all countries,
#    the model is robust to this source of structural uncertainty.
#
# 3. CROSS-COUNTRY TRANSFERABILITY:
#    Compare how cost-effectiveness varies by country under both
#    distributional assumptions.

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: CHECK WHICH COUNTRY WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA RESULTS ARE AVAILABLE
# ============================================================================

# Define file paths for each country's Weibull vs Gamma PSA comparison
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
file_wvg_ireland <- file.path("output", "Weibull_vs_Gamma_Ireland_PSA.csv")
file_wvg_germany <- file.path("output", "Weibull_vs_Gamma_Germany_PSA.csv")
file_wvg_spain <- file.path("output", "Weibull_vs_Gamma_Spain_PSA.csv")

# Check which files exist
# -----------------------
exists_wvg_ireland <- file.exists(file_wvg_ireland)
exists_wvg_germany <- file.exists(file_wvg_germany)
exists_wvg_spain <- file.exists(file_wvg_spain)

# Display which country results are available
# --------------------------------------------
cat("\n=======================================================\n")
cat("CONSOLIDATING WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA RESULTS ACROSS COUNTRIES\n")
cat("=======================================================\n\n")
cat("Checking for available Weibull vs Gamma PSA files...\n\n")

# Report availability status for each country
cat("Ireland:", ifelse(exists_wvg_ireland, "✓ Available", "✗ Not yet generated"), "\n")
cat("Germany:", ifelse(exists_wvg_germany, "✓ Available", "✗ Not yet generated"), "\n")
cat("Spain:  ", ifelse(exists_wvg_spain, "✓ Available", "✗ Not yet generated"), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: LOAD AVAILABLE COUNTRY WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA RESULTS
# ============================================================================

# Initialize empty list to store country data frames
wvg_list <- list()

# Define WTP thresholds for each country (for reference in consolidated table)
# These match the values defined in each country's parameter file
wtp_ireland <- 45000
wtp_germany <- 78871
wtp_spain <- 30000

# Load Ireland data if available
if (exists_wvg_ireland) {
  df_wvg_ireland <- read.csv(file_wvg_ireland, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df_wvg_ireland$Country <- "Ireland"
  df_wvg_ireland$WTP_Threshold <- wtp_ireland
  wvg_list[["Ireland"]] <- df_wvg_ireland
  cat("✓ Loaded Ireland Weibull vs Gamma PSA results (", nrow(df_wvg_ireland), " rows)\n")
}

# Load Germany data if available
if (exists_wvg_germany) {
  df_wvg_germany <- read.csv(file_wvg_germany, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df_wvg_germany$Country <- "Germany"
  df_wvg_germany$WTP_Threshold <- wtp_germany
  wvg_list[["Germany"]] <- df_wvg_germany
  cat("✓ Loaded Germany Weibull vs Gamma PSA results (", nrow(df_wvg_germany), " rows)\n")
}

# Load Spain data if available
if (exists_wvg_spain) {
  df_wvg_spain <- read.csv(file_wvg_spain, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df_wvg_spain$Country <- "Spain"
  df_wvg_spain$WTP_Threshold <- wtp_spain
  wvg_list[["Spain"]] <- df_wvg_spain
  cat("✓ Loaded Spain Weibull vs Gamma PSA results (", nrow(df_wvg_spain), " rows)\n")
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: COMBINE COUNTRY RESULTS INTO CONSOLIDATED TABLE
# ============================================================================

if (length(wvg_list) > 0) {
  # Combine all available country data frames
  wvg_consolidated <- do.call(rbind, wvg_list)

  # Reorder columns to put Country and WTP_Threshold first
  # This makes the table easier to read and interpret
  col_order <- c("Country", "WTP_Threshold", "Distribution",
                 setdiff(names(wvg_consolidated), c("Country", "WTP_Threshold", "Distribution")))
  wvg_consolidated <- wvg_consolidated[, col_order]

  # Remove row names for cleaner output
  rownames(wvg_consolidated) <- NULL

  cat("\n=======================================================\n")
  cat("CONSOLIDATED WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA TABLE\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("Countries included:", length(wvg_list), "\n")
  cat("Total rows:", nrow(wvg_consolidated), "(2 per country: Weibull + Gamma)\n\n")

  # Display the consolidated table
  print(wvg_consolidated, row.names = FALSE)

} else {
  cat("\n=======================================================\n")
  cat("WARNING: NO WEIBULL VS GAMMA PSA FILES FOUND\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("Please run the PSA analysis for at least one country first.\n")
  cat("This will generate the Weibull_vs_Gamma_<country>_PSA.csv files.\n\n")
  wvg_consolidated <- data.frame()
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: SAVE CONSOLIDATED TABLE TO CSV
# ============================================================================

if (nrow(wvg_consolidated) > 0) {

  # Define output file path
  wvg_consolidated_file <- file.path("output", "Weibull_vs_Gamma_All_Countries_PSA.csv")

  # Write to CSV
  write.csv(
    wvg_consolidated,
    file = wvg_consolidated_file,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  cat("\n=======================================================\n")
  cat("FILE SAVED SUCCESSFULLY\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("Consolidated Weibull vs Gamma PSA results saved to:\n")
  cat("  ", wvg_consolidated_file, "\n\n")

  # ============================================================================
  # STEP 5: INTERPRET CROSS-COUNTRY STRUCTURAL UNCERTAINTY
  # ============================================================================

  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("CROSS-COUNTRY STRUCTURAL UNCERTAINTY SUMMARY\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n\n")

  # For each country, compare Weibull vs Gamma ICERs
  for (country in unique(wvg_consolidated$Country)) {
    country_data <- wvg_consolidated[wvg_consolidated$Country == country, ]

    weibull_icer <- country_data$ICER_PSA[country_data$Distribution == "Weibull"]
    gamma_icer <- country_data$ICER_PSA[country_data$Distribution == "Gamma"]
    wtp <- country_data$WTP_Threshold[1]

    if (length(weibull_icer) > 0 && length(gamma_icer) > 0) {
      icer_diff <- gamma_icer - weibull_icer
      icer_pct_change <- (gamma_icer - weibull_icer) / weibull_icer * 100

      cat(country, " (WTP: €", format(wtp, big.mark = ","), "):\n", sep = "")
      cat("  Weibull ICER: €", format(round(weibull_icer, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n", sep = "")
      cat("  Gamma ICER:   €", format(round(gamma_icer, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n", sep = "")
      cat("  Difference:   €", format(round(icer_diff, 0), big.mark = ","),
          " (", round(icer_pct_change, 1), "%)\n", sep = "")

      # Check if conclusion changes
      weibull_ce <- weibull_icer <= wtp
      gamma_ce <- gamma_icer <= wtp

      if (weibull_ce == gamma_ce) {
        if (weibull_ce) {
          cat("  Conclusion:   Cost-effective under BOTH distributions\n\n")
        } else {
          cat("  Conclusion:   NOT cost-effective under EITHER distribution\n\n")
        }
      } else {
        cat("  Conclusion:   **CHANGES with distribution choice**\n\n")
      }
    }
  }

  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat("WEIBULL VS GAMMA ALL COUNTRIES CONSOLIDATION COMPLETE\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n\n")

} else {
  cat("No consolidated file created (no data available).\n\n")
}

```

```{r}

#09.2 Create PSA object for dampack

# Dampack has a number of functions to summarise and visualise the results of a probabilistic sensitivity analysis. However, the data needs to be in a specific structure before we can use those functions. 

# The 'dampack' package contains multiple useful functions that summarize and visualize the results of a
# probabilitic analysis. To use those functions, the data has to be in a particular structure.
l_PA <- make_psa_obj(cost          = df_c, 
                     effectiveness = df_e, 
                     parameters    = df_PA_input, 
                     strategies    = c("SoC", "Bev"),
                        currency = "€")

# So, basically we make a psa object for Dampack where df_c is the dataframe of costs from the Markov model being applied to the PSA data, and df_e is the data.frame of effectiveness from the Markov model being applied to the PSA dataset, the parameters that are included are those from the PSA analysis, which we fed into df_PA_input above (df_PA_input<-) and the two strategies are SoC and Exp.

# I added the "currency" section to the above so that my PSA plots would stop printing out with dollar signs, per this link: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dampack/vignettes/psa_analysis.html also available here: web.archive.org/web/20220802010424/https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dampack/vignettes/psa_analysis.html

# Also, initially the above was strategies    = c("SoC", "Exp"), but I changed this to strategies    = c("SoC", "Bev"), as the scatter plot and CEAC diagrams produced then had Bev written on them under strategies instead of Exp, which made what we were doing a lot clearer.


```

```{r}
#09.3.1 Conduct CEA with probabilistic output

# First we take the mean outcome estimates, that is, we summarise the expected costs and effects for each strategy from the PSA:
(df_out_ce_PA <- summary(l_PA))


# Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs)

# Then we calculate the ICERs from this df_out_ce_PA (summary must be a dampack function doing things under the hood to create a selectable ($) meanCost, meanEffect and Strategy parameter in df_out_ce_PA):
(df_cea_PA <- calculate_icers(cost       = df_out_ce_PA$meanCost, 
                              effect     = df_out_ce_PA$meanEffect,
                              strategies = df_out_ce_PA$Strategy))

# We can view the ICER results from the PSA here:
df_cea_PA

# If we wanted to save the CEA (or leauge) table with ICERs, we would do this as follows:

#     file = "markov_3state_probabilistic_CEA_results.RData")
# As .csv
# write.csv(df_cea_pa, 
#          file = "markov_3state_probabilistic_CEA_results.csv")


## CEA table in proper format ---- per: C:\Users\Jonathan\OneDrive - Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland\COLOSSUS\Training Resources\R-HTA in LMICs Intermediate R-HTA Modelling Tutorial\September-Workshop-main\September-Workshop-main\analysis\cSTM_time_dep_simulation.r
table_cea_PA <- format_table_cea(df_cea_PA) # Function included in "R/Functions.R"; depends on the `scales` package
table_cea_PA
```

```{r}
#09.3.2 Cost-Effectiveness Scatter plot

# Incremental cost-effectiveness plane

# I wanted my scatterplots to have a title reflecting the country they were for, so I commented out the below:

# plot(l_PA)
# ggsave(paste("CE_Scatter_Plot_", country_name[1], ".png", sep = ""), width = 8, height = 4, dpi=300)
# while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()


# I'd like to add a title to the plot "Scatter Plot country_name" where country_name is the name of the country that country_name is currently equal to, this can be Spain, Germany or Ireland.

# To add a title to my cost-effectiveness scatter plot using ggplot2, I modify the plot object created by plot(l_PA) to include a title.

# I Create the plot object using plot(l_PA):
ce_scatter_plot <- plot(l_PA, ylim = c(0, 200000))

# I add a the title to the plot object using ggtitle (as before the title will be centered above the plot):
plot_title <- paste("Scatter Plot", country_name)
ce_scatter_plot <- ce_scatter_plot + ggtitle(plot_title) + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Save the plot to a file
ggsave(file.path("output", paste("CE_Scatter_Plot_", country_name[1], ".png", sep = "")), plot = ce_scatter_plot, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 600)

# Close the graphics device
while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()

# Because I'm setting limits to put everything on the same range without actually knowing how these limits fit with the actual data, I create two versions of this plot, one with the limits applied, and one without the limits applied, so I can compare the two plots produced:

unlimited_ce_scatter_plot <- plot(l_PA)
plot_title <- paste("Scatter Plot", country_name)
unlimited_ce_scatter_plot <- unlimited_ce_scatter_plot + ggtitle(plot_title) + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
ggsave(file.path("output", paste("Unlimited_CE_Scatter_Plot_", country_name[1], ".png", sep = "")), plot = unlimited_ce_scatter_plot, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 600)
while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()

#plot(l_PA, xlim = c(9.5, 22.5))
# In the DARTH package R code they use the additional bits above, I can see how they look in my own model, and if I'd like to use them.

# In this plot, it would be easy to get caught off guard by the fact that some of the effectiveness values are above 1, however, in health economics, Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALYs) are not inherently bound by 1. QALYs are used as a measure that combines the quantity and quality of life lived, and they are typically used in cost-utility analyses to assess the value for money of medical interventions.

#Here are a few key points to understand about QALYs:

# Calculation: QALYs are calculated by multiplying the duration of time spent in a health state by the quality of life score (utility value) associated with that health state. Utility values typically range from 0 to 1, where:

# 0 represents a health state equivalent to death.
# 1 represents perfect health.

# Beyond One Year: Since QALYs represent both the quality and quantity of life, they can exceed 1 if the time period considered is more than one year. For example, 2 years in perfect health would equal 2 QALYs (2 years * 1 utility = 2 QALYs).

# Utility Values: While utility values are generally between 0 and 1, in some cases, they can be negative, representing health states considered worse than death. This means that the QALYs for a period spent in such a state could be negative.

# Lifetime QALYs: Over a person's lifetime, the total QALYs accumulated can be much greater than 1, depending on the length of life and the quality of health throughout that period.

# In summary, while the utility value for any given health state is typically between 0 and 1, the total QALYs can exceed 1 since they are a cumulative measure over time.

# This is supported by: https://www.scottishmedicines.org.uk/media/2839/guide-to-qalys.pdf

```

```{r}
#09.4.2 Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves (CEACs) and frontier (CEAF)

# Cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC):

# We first generate a vector of willingness to pay values (thresholds) to define for which values the CEAC is made:
v_wtp <- seq(0, 500000, by = 10000)
# This basically gives you a sequence of willingness to pay thresholds from 0 all the way up to 500,000 euro, increasing by 10,000 euro each time, so start with 0 euro, go to 10,000 euro, go to 20,000 euro, and so on until you hit 500,000. You can chose any max value you like and any increment value you like, for example, in the DARTH material they use the following: v_wtp <- seq(0, 45000, by = 1000)
CEAC_obj <- ceac(wtp = v_wtp, psa = l_PA)

summary(CEAC_obj)
```

## 08.3.3 Table Describing Parameters

To build a Table describing parameters, you click on the Table button at the top, and design it in there.
Then to include the parameter values automatically as they are updated you fill in the parameter name you want, highlight it in the cell and click \</\> from above to put it in a code block.
You do the same for gamma, etc., put this in code blocks also.
<https://rpruim.github.io/s341/S19/from-class/MathinRmd.html#:~:text=Math%20inside%20RMarkdown,10n%3D1n2.>

Per: [Putting the value of a variable into a table in R Markdown, rather than it's name - Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72902548/putting-the-value-of-a-variable-into-a-table-in-r-markdown-rather-than-its-nam)

Line 320 of this: <https://github.com/DARTH-git/cohort-modeling-tutorial-intro/blob/main/manuscript/cSTM_Tutorial_Intro.Rmd> is informative when viewing the final document on page 7 here: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.07824.pdf>

Some helpful tips on using math notation in R Markdown.

<https://rpruim.github.io/s341/S19/from-class/MathinRmd.html>

This paper says in technical terms which distributions fit and why:

```{r}
#===============================================================================
# SCENARIO ANALYSIS: RAMSEY BASE CASE VS POPULATION NORM ADJUSTED UTILITIES
#===============================================================================

# CONTEXT: Addressing Reviewer 2 Concern About Utility Values
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# This chunk runs the deterministic cost-effectiveness model for ALL countries
# (Ireland, Germany, Spain) under BOTH utility scenarios:
#   1. Ramsey base case (0.85, 0.65)
#   2. Population norm adjusted (mCRC multipliers × country/age norms)
#
# OUTPUT: CSV file with side-by-side comparison of cost-effectiveness results
#
# This directly addresses the reviewer concern that Ramsey utilities may
# exceed population norms and demonstrates robustness of conclusions.

cat("\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("RUNNING UTILITY SCENARIO ANALYSIS FOR ALL COUNTRIES\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("\n")

# STEP 1: Define countries, scenarios, and parameter storage
# -----------------------------------------------------------
countries_to_analyze <- c("Ireland", "Germany", "Spain")
# List of all countries in the analysis

scenarios_to_run <- c("ramsey_basecase", "population_norm_adjusted")
# List of utility scenarios to compare

patient_age_for_analysis <- 65
# Representative age for mCRC patients (used for population norm lookup)

# Initialize results data frame
# ------------------------------
scenario_results_df <- data.frame()
# Empty data frame to store results
# Will be populated row-by-row for each (country, scenario) combination


# STEP 2: Loop over countries and scenarios
# ------------------------------------------
for (ctry in countries_to_analyze) {
  # Outer loop: iterate over countries

  cat("\n")
  cat("========================================================================\n")
  cat("COUNTRY:", ctry, "\n")
  cat("========================================================================\n")

  # Set country-specific parameters using helper function
  # ------------------------------------------------------
  # The get_country_params() function (defined earlier in this document)
  # returns all country-specific costs, WTP threshold, and discount rates.
  # This ensures consistency across all analyses and avoids hard-coding values.

  params_ctry <- get_country_params(ctry)

  # Extract country-specific parameters
  c_PFS_Folfox_ctry <- params_ctry$c_PFS_Folfox
  c_PFS_Bevacizumab_ctry <- params_ctry$c_PFS_Bevacizumab
  c_OS_Folfiri_ctry <- params_ctry$c_OS_Folfiri
  administration_cost_ctry <- params_ctry$administration_cost
  subtyping_test_cost_ctry <- params_ctry$subtyping_test_cost
  c_AE1_ctry <- params_ctry$c_AE1
  c_AE2_ctry <- params_ctry$c_AE2
  c_AE3_ctry <- params_ctry$c_AE3
  n_wtp_ctry <- params_ctry$n_wtp
  d_c_ctry <- params_ctry$country_discount_rate
  d_e_ctry <- params_ctry$country_discount_rate  # Assume same rate for costs and effects

  for (scen in scenarios_to_run) {
    # Inner loop: iterate over scenarios for this country

    cat("\n")
    cat("  Scenario:", scen, "\n")
    cat("  ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n")

    # STEP 3: Get utilities for this scenario
    # ----------------------------------------
    utility_result_scen <- get_utility_scenario(
      country = ctry,                      # Current country
      age = patient_age_for_analysis,      # Patient age (65)
      utility_scenario = scen,             # Current scenario
      df_popnorm = df_popnorm              # Population norms data
    )
    # Returns list with u_PFS, u_PD, and metadata

    u_F_scen <- utility_result_scen$u_PFS
    # PFS utility for this scenario
    # Example: Ireland ramsey_basecase → 0.85
    #          Ireland population_norm_adjusted → ~0.80 (depends on multipliers)

    u_P_scen <- utility_result_scen$u_PD
    # PD utility for this scenario
    # Example: Ireland ramsey_basecase → 0.65
    #          Ireland population_norm_adjusted → ~0.70 (depends on multipliers)

    cat("    u_PFS:", round(u_F_scen, 4), "\n")
    cat("    u_PD: ", round(u_P_scen, 4), "\n")

    # STEP 4: Build parameter list for model run
    # -------------------------------------------
    # We need to construct l_params_all with all model parameters,
    # using the country-specific costs and scenario-specific utilities.
    #
    # NOTE: This assumes all other parameters (hazard ratios, AE probabilities, etc.)
    #       are already defined in the environment from earlier chunks.
    #       In a production implementation, you would ensure all parameters are
    #       explicitly included here or passed via a helper function.

    l_params_scen <- list(
      # Hazard ratios (assumed already defined earlier)
      HR_FP_Exp = HR_FP_Exp,
      HR_FP_SoC = HR_FP_SoC,
      HR_PD_Exp = HR_PD_Exp,
      HR_PD_SoC = HR_PD_SoC,
      P_OSD_SoC = P_OSD_SoC,
      P_OSD_Exp = P_OSD_Exp,

      # Adverse event probabilities (assumed already defined earlier)
      p_FA1_STD = p_FA1_STD,
      p_FA2_STD = p_FA2_STD,
      p_FA3_STD = p_FA3_STD,
      p_FA1_EXPR = p_FA1_EXPR,
      p_FA2_EXPR = p_FA2_EXPR,
      p_FA3_EXPR = p_FA3_EXPR,
      p_OSA1_FOLFIRI = p_OSA1_FOLFIRI,
      p_OSA2_FOLFIRI = p_OSA2_FOLFIRI,
      p_OSA3_FOLFIRI = p_OSA3_FOLFIRI,

      # Country-specific costs
      administration_cost = administration_cost_ctry,
      c_PFS_Folfox = c_PFS_Folfox_ctry,
      c_PFS_Bevacizumab = c_PFS_Bevacizumab_ctry,
      c_OS_Folfiri = c_OS_Folfiri_ctry,
      c_AE1 = c_AE1_ctry,
      c_AE2 = c_AE2_ctry,
      c_AE3 = c_AE3_ctry,

      # Scenario-specific utilities
      u_F = u_F_scen,
      u_P = u_P_scen,
      u_D = 0,

      # Adverse event disutilities (assumed already defined earlier)
      AE1_DisUtil = AE1_DisUtil,
      AE2_DisUtil = AE2_DisUtil,
      AE3_DisUtil = AE3_DisUtil,

      # Country-specific discount rates (converted to daily for 14-day cycles)
      # NOTE: Annual rates must be converted to daily rates because the model
      #       uses 14-day cycles with t_cycle = 14 days. The discounting formula
      #       v_dwc <- 1 / ((1 + d_c) ^ ((0:(n_cycle-1)) * t_cycle))
      #       multiplies the discount rate by t_cycle (in days), so d_c and d_e
      #       must be in daily units for correct discounting over the time horizon.
      d_e = d_e_ctry / 365,
      d_c = d_c_ctry / 365,

      # Other parameters (assumed already defined earlier)
      n_cycle = n_cycle,
      t_cycle = t_cycle,

      # Survival curve coefficients (assumed already defined earlier)
      # These would come from the survival analysis section
      # For Weibull (base case):
      coef_weibull_shape_SoC = coef_weibull_shape_SoC,
      coef_weibull_scale_SoC = coef_weibull_scale_SoC,
      coef_TTD_weibull_shape_SoC = coef_TTD_weibull_shape_SoC,
      coef_TTD_weibull_scale_SoC = coef_TTD_weibull_scale_SoC
    )

    # STEP 5: Run the oncologySemiMarkov model
    # -----------------------------------------
    result_scen <- oncologySemiMarkov(
      l_params_all = l_params_scen,
      n_wtp = n_wtp_ctry,
      curve_choice = "weibull"  # Use Weibull as base case (can change to "gamma" for sensitivity)
    )
    # Returns a data frame with columns: Strategy, Cost, Effect, DSAICER
    # Row 1: Standard of Care (SoC)
    # Row 2: Experimental Treatment (Exp)

    # STEP 6: Extract results
    # ------------------------
    cost_soc_scen <- result_scen$Cost[1]
    # Total discounted cost for SoC strategy

    cost_exp_scen <- result_scen$Cost[2]
    # Total discounted cost for Exp strategy

    qaly_soc_scen <- result_scen$Effect[1]
    # Total discounted QALYs for SoC strategy

    qaly_exp_scen <- result_scen$Effect[2]
    # Total discounted QALYs for Exp strategy

    inc_cost_scen <- cost_exp_scen - cost_soc_scen
    # Incremental cost (Exp - SoC)

    inc_qaly_scen <- qaly_exp_scen - qaly_soc_scen
    # Incremental QALYs (Exp - SoC)

    icer_scen <- inc_cost_scen / inc_qaly_scen
    # Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (€ per QALY gained)

    nmb_scen <- (inc_qaly_scen * n_wtp_ctry) - inc_cost_scen
    # Net monetary benefit at country-specific WTP threshold
    # Positive NMB → intervention is cost-effective at this WTP
    # Negative NMB → intervention is NOT cost-effective at this WTP

    # Print results for this scenario
    cat("    Cost SoC:     €", round(cost_soc_scen, 2), "\n")
    cat("    Cost Exp:     €", round(cost_exp_scen, 2), "\n")
    cat("    QALY SoC:     ", round(qaly_soc_scen, 4), "\n")
    cat("    QALY Exp:     ", round(qaly_exp_scen, 4), "\n")
    cat("    Incr Cost:    €", round(inc_cost_scen, 2), "\n")
    cat("    Incr QALY:    ", round(inc_qaly_scen, 4), "\n")
    cat("    ICER:         €", round(icer_scen, 2), " per QALY\n")
    cat("    NMB (at WTP €", n_wtp_ctry, "): €", round(nmb_scen, 2), "\n", sep="")

    if (nmb_scen > 0) {
      cat("    → COST-EFFECTIVE at this WTP threshold\n")
    } else {
      cat("    → NOT COST-EFFECTIVE at this WTP threshold\n")
    }

    # STEP 7: Store results in data frame
    # ------------------------------------
    result_row <- data.frame(
      Country = ctry,
      Scenario = scen,
      u_PFS = u_F_scen,
      u_PD = u_P_scen,
      Cost_SoC = cost_soc_scen,
      Cost_Exp = cost_exp_scen,
      QALY_SoC = qaly_soc_scen,
      QALY_Exp = qaly_exp_scen,
      Inc_Cost = inc_cost_scen,
      Inc_QALY = inc_qaly_scen,
      ICER = icer_scen,
      WTP = n_wtp_ctry,
      NMB = nmb_scen,
      Cost_Effective = ifelse(nmb_scen > 0, "Yes", "No"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    scenario_results_df <- rbind(scenario_results_df, result_row)
    # Append this row to the results data frame
  }
}

cat("\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("SCENARIO ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("\n")

# STEP 8: Print summary table
# ----------------------------
cat("SUMMARY TABLE: RAMSEY BASE CASE VS POPULATION NORM ADJUSTED\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
print(scenario_results_df, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n")

# STEP 9: Write results to CSV
# -----------------------------
# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists("output")) {
  dir.create("output")
  cat("Created output/ directory\n")
}

# Write CSV file
output_file <- "output/Utility_Scenario_Summary.csv"
write.csv(scenario_results_df, file = output_file, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Results written to:", output_file, "\n")
cat("\n")
```
